thread:
incident-bot: INCIDENT: p95 latency spike detected in hosted-eu-1 (models endpoint). Paging @oncall-ryan @sre-anna. Auto-created channel: #inc-4310001234

oncall-ryan: Ack, I'm on it. Seeing alerts for increased p95 and error budget burn. Initial impact: webhooks & sync inference slow, some 504s.

sre-anna: Confirming dashboards — p50 moved 120ms -> 160ms, p95 jumped 420ms -> 1.8s in the last 8m. Token rate steady.

eng-runtime-julia: Did any deploys go out in eu region in the last 30m?

infra-luis: No infra deploys. We had a kernel security backport on eu hosts 45m ago (hotfix-5.18.21).

oncall-ryan: Copy. Could be related. Let's gather traces and perf counters. @eng-kernel-max can you look at kernel perf events?

eng-kernel-max: Checking perf data now. Running: `sudo perf stat -a -e context-switches,cpu-migrations -p $(pgrep -f redwood-runtime)`

support-olivia: Customer impact: two enterprise customers reported longer inference times and 3 customers saw <1% increase in failed requests. Notified CSMs.

pm-kate: Heads-up to sales ops — we may need a short incident banner. Prioritize timeline and root cause.

eng-runtime-julia: Sharing traces from the trace sampler (recent 20):
```
span_id: 0x1c3a
service: runtime-host
root: model.generate
duration_ms: 1845
children: kv-cache-lookup(12ms), token-gen(1700ms), syscall(120ms)
```
Most long spans show token-gen waiting on syscalls around context switch bursts.

sre-anna: I'm dumping top stacks on the busy processes: `pprof top` shows high time in `sched_yield` and `__switch_to`.

eng-kernel-max: Perf counters show context-switches increased 6x on affected hosts. cpu-steal minimal. This aligns with scheduler churn.

infra-luis: Host list affected: eu-gpu-1[04-08], eu-gpu-2[01-03] — all had the kernel hotfix applied. Rolling back to previous kernel on one host for test?

oncall-ryan: Do not roll back cluster-wide yet. Let's test rollback on eu-gpu-104 (canary). If it improves p95, we have a causal lever.

eng-runtime-julia: Mitigations in parallel: 1) scale up dedicated pool (add 8 nodes), 2) enable model-variant fallback (smaller quantized model) for non-enterprise traffic, 3) pause background rebalances. Doing scale now: `infra scale --pool hosted-eu-1 --add 8`

incident-bot: Action taken: scaled hosted-eu-1 by +8 nodes (initiated).

support-olivia: Applying fallback policy to non-SLA routes now (will cut some latency for non-enterprise traffic).

oncall-ryan: Rolling kernel rollback to eu-gpu-104 now (maintenance window). Watch metrics.

eng-kernel-max: Rollback complete on eu-gpu-104. Rebooted and runtime back up.

sre-anna: Quick check: p95 on eu-gpu-104 instance series dropped from 1.7s -> 340ms within 90s of boot. Other hosts still high.

eng-runtime-julia: Traces from the rolled-back host show token-gen back to normal distribution; syscall waiting gone.

infra-luis: Proceeding with phased rollback across remaining affected hosts. Will do in waves of 2 to avoid capacity loss.

pm-kate: Good signal. Prepare a short incident banner: "Investigating increased inference latency in EU region; mitigation in progress." I'll draft.

support-olivia: Customer comms queued. Will update customers who reported issues.

oncall-ryan: Timeline notes for RCA: 
- T-45m: kernel hotfix-5.18.21 rollout started to eu hosts
- T-30m: first p95 increase detected by alerting
- T0: incident created and paged oncall
- T+8m: traces & perf indicate scheduler churn/context-switch spike on affected hosts
- T+20m: rollback canary applied to eu-gpu-104 -> p95 improved
- T+30-60m: phased rollback in progress, capacity scale and fallback enabled (mitigations)

eng-kernel-max: Hypothesis: kernel scheduler change in hotfix increases wake-up latencies for the GPU runtime threads under our workload, causing extra context-switch noise and token generation stalls.

eng-runtime-julia: Corroborating: the runtime's busy-wait loop is more sensitive to scheduler wake jitter; we see more syscalls returning with EINTR spikes.

sre-anna: Saved logs & perf data to /var/reports/inc-4310001234/perf.tar.gz and uploaded to S3: s3://redwood-incidents/4310001234/perf.tar.gz

oncall-ryan: Actions next: (1) finish rollback, (2) keep scaled capacity until end of hour, (3) create RCA doc with timeline, perf data, traces, and mitigation steps. Assign eng-kernel-max + eng-runtime-julia for joint RCA.

eng-kernel-max: Will prepare kernel-side diff and reproduce steps. Planning to open a kernel backport test PR and coordinate with infra.

eng-runtime-julia: I'll add synthetic load tests to reproduce scheduler sensitivity and evaluate runtime-side mitigations (e.g., tight spin vs futex).

pm-kate: Assigning PM follow-ups: incident postmortem, customer notes, and possible SLA credits checklist.

incident-bot: Incident state: mitigated -> rolling. Next update in 15m or on completion of rollback.

oncall-ryan: Thanks team. Keep posts short and paste logs/traces here as needed. If anything changes (errors or increased customer reports) ping @pm-kate immediately. :thumbsup:

eng-runtime-julia: Paste: recent trace sample from problematic host:
```
span: model.generate token-gen
duration: 1802ms
stack: runtime->futex_wait->__switch_to->sched_yield
```
This aligns with kernel scheduler stalls.

sre-anna: Updating timeline doc with the above. Continuing monitoring.

support-olivia: Customers notified of ongoing mitigations; will send follow-up once rollback completes.

(End of thread)
